title: 2005 AMC 8 Problem 7
statement: Bill walks \(\frac{1}{2}\) mile south, then \(\frac{3}{4}\) mile east, and finally \(\frac{1}{2}\) mile south. How many miles is he, in a direct line, from his starting point?

solutions.text:
Note that what we want is the length of the diagonal. We can use the Pythagorean theorem to find this. \[ \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}^2} \] \[ = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{9}{16}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{16}} = \dfrac{5}{4} \]

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Combine the two southward parts into one vertical displacement.
Use the Pythagorean theorem with legs \(1\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\).
